statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 14% because the observed US session path keeps rotating inside its own range: NQ trades 29,144.75 roughly 68 points below the 29,213.00 session high, NDX cash is 29,100.33 after fading from 29,165.62, and VIX has slipped to a new session low of 15.40 against a 16.82 high. Stress eases to 60% as the curve sits flat with the 10Y at 4.796% and the 2Y at 4.39%, but stays elevated on WTI at $91.08, the Hormuz backdrop and the after-close Broadcom print.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, reflecting observed two-way price discovery and decaying implied volatility rather than any resolution of the macro backdrop. Tail remains below the block threshold for most of the next 24 hours; forecast Tail crosses it only inside the narrow 20:00-23:00 UTC window covering the Broadcom results, the 21:00 UTC management call and the 22:00 UTC futures reopen. Single-hour watch-band checkpoints sit at the 18:00 UTC Beige Book and across the Thursday 12:00-15:00 UTC block containing jobless claims, the US cash open and ISM Services. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 rotates inside its range as VIX prints a session low of 15.40 and the Treasury curve sits flat
body:
Four hours into the US cash session the price path is a range rotation rather than a trend. NQ futures trade 29,144.75, up 19.25 points or 0.07% from the 29,125.50 previous close, inside a 28,927.25 to 29,213.00 day range on Yahoo Finance. The cash Nasdaq-100 stands at 29,100.33, up 23.11 points or 0.08%, against a 28,971.90 to 29,165.62 range, having faded back from its own session high. Both the 28,927.25 low and the 29,213.00 high have now been left behind without a follow-through leg, which is the direct opposite of the repeated extension after failed pullbacks that this Tail score measures. Tail steps down again from 15% to 14%.

Cross-asset evidence supports the same reading. VIX is 15.40, down 5.75%, printing a new session low against a 16.82 high; implied volatility is decaying rather than building. The Treasury curve is essentially unchanged, with the 10-year at 4.796% flat on the day inside a 4.768 to 4.806 range and the 2-year easing to 4.39%, so there is no aligned rates-plus-equities impulse of the kind that would amplify a directional path. Crude is the one factor still firming: WTI trades $91.08, up 0.95%, with Brent near $95 after the EIA reported a 4.45 million barrel crude draw against a 1.1 million consensus. Factory orders rose 0.9% against a 0.6% consensus.

The macro backdrop is the reason Stress stays elevated at 60% rather than falling with Tail. August ADP printed 38,000 against a 47,000 consensus, the slowest month since January, while markets still price roughly two-thirds odds of a hike at the 15-16 September meeting. New York Fed President John Williams said in a CNBC interview today that the yield surge reflects a strong economy rather than dysfunction and that there are no clear signs yet that a September move is necessary. A 10-year near its highest since 2023, crude near $91 on the Strait of Hormuz backdrop, Broadcom's after-close report and Friday's payrolls together keep the environment difficult even while intraday mean reversion is functioning normally.

Mapped policy state is EA_ON. The narrow danger window is 20:00 to 23:00 UTC, widened by one hour from the previous assessment to cover the Broadcom results after the 20:00 UTC cash close, the 21:00 UTC management call that runs inside the CME maintenance halt, and the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen where a single-step gap is most credible. Broadcom fell about 13% after its previous report despite beating estimates, so guidance rather than the headline print is the swing variable. Single-hour watch-band checkpoints sit at the 18:00 UTC Beige Book and across the Thursday block containing jobless claims at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC cash open and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment moved from the orange band during Tuesday's yield-and-oil driven selloff, through a long stretch of watch-band event/whipsaw readings overnight, into the green band from 12:00 UTC as the US session produced an orderly two-way recovery. Tail has fallen from 25% at 19:00 UTC yesterday to 15% at the 15:00 UTC assessment, with Stress easing from 77% to 61% over the same span. Three hours are marked unavailable: 20:00 and 01:00 UTC, where no assessment was published, and 16:00 UTC, where the scheduled run produced no snapshot.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are shaped by one concentrated corporate catalyst and one macro block. Forecast Tail stays in the low band through the afternoon, steps into the watch band for the 18:00 UTC Beige Book and the final cash hour, then crosses the block threshold across 20:00 to 23:00 UTC for the Broadcom release, the management call inside the futures maintenance halt and the 22:00 UTC reopen. Overnight the conditional path returns to the low band through the Asian and European sessions, before a second watch-band block on Thursday covering jobless claims at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC US cash open and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC. Stress remains in the elevated band throughout on firm crude, a 10-year near multi-year highs and Friday's payroll print ahead of the September policy meeting.

forecast.analysis: Broadcom's management call begins at 21:00 UTC (14:00 Pacific) while CME equity futures sit in their daily maintenance halt, so AI-order and gross-margin commentary is absorbed without a continuous index price path. This is the classic delayed second-leg structure, and forecast Tail is highest here for the whole 24-hour window.

CME equity index futures in their 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt
Guidance above $29.25B and AI-order commentary are the swing variables
Delayed second-leg mechanism: commentary absorbed without continuous pricing

forecast.analysis: Globex reopens at 22:00 UTC and would reprice the Broadcom call in a single step, so this is the hour in which an opening gap could extend without offering a meaningful pullback. Tail stays above the block threshold conditionally. A reopen that trades back into the 28,927.25-29,213.00 range would be the first sign the gap is being absorbed.
drivers: CME equity futures reopen at 22:00 UTC after the maintenance halt
Reopening gap can extend before two-way liquidity returns
Invalidation: an early return inside the 28,927.25-29,213.00 range
Semiconductor read-across from Broadcom guidance is the dominant driver

forecast.analysis: First digestion hour after the Broadcom reopen. Conditional Tail steps back to the watch band on the assumption that the initial repricing has largely occurred and early Asian liquidity begins to provide two-way flow. A second directional leg on the call transcript rather than the headline numbers is the main way this hour stays stressed.
drivers: Post-reopen digestion of the Broadcom release and call
Checkpoint: whether early Asian liquidity restores two-way flow
Risk of a second leg driven by the transcript rather than the headline print
Semiconductor complex remains the index-level transmission channel

forecast.analysis: Asian handover with no scheduled US release. The published path assumes Broadcom repricing has been absorbed and volatility resumes decaying, returning Tail to the low band. Persistent one-way extension carried through the Tokyo open would invalidate that assumption and is the condition to monitor rather than a state assumed to exist.
drivers: Asian session handover with no scheduled US macro release
Assumption: Broadcom repricing largely absorbed before Tokyo
Invalidation: one-way extension persisting through the Asian open

forecast.analysis: Quiet Asian hours. With the September FOMC still two weeks out and no release scheduled, conditional Tail sits in the low band. Stress stays in the elevated band because crude near $91 and a 10Y near 4.80% keep the macro backdrop tight even when the intraday path is orderly and mean reversion functions normally.
drivers: No scheduled US macro release inside this hour
WTI near $91 keeps the energy-inflation channel open
10Y near 4.80% sustains elevated Stress without implying a Tail path

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian session. The published path assumes range behaviour with mean reversion intact. Overnight crude headlines out of the Strait of Hormuz remain the main way a low-liquidity hour turns directional, so an energy-led gap is the specific condition that would lift this slot rather than generic overnight volatility.

No scheduled US release; conditional path only

Asian semiconductor supplier performance is the most direct hourly checkpoint for whether that assumption survives into the European handover.
drivers: Asian semiconductor suppliers as the Broadcom read-across checkpoint
Assumption: no index-level trend carried out of the Asian session
No scheduled US macro release inside this hour

forecast.analysis: Asia-to-Europe transition, historically the calmest window of the 24-hour cycle. With no catalyst scheduled and volatility assumed to have decayed further, conditional Tail sits at the low end. The published score would only rise if the overnight range had already been broken with no retracement by this point.
drivers: Asia-to-Europe transition with no scheduled catalyst
Conditional low-band score assumes an intact overnight range

forecast.analysis: Pre-European hours remain the low point of conditional risk. Stress holds in the elevated band purely on the standing macro backdrop of firm crude, a 10Y near multi-year highs and Friday payrolls ahead, not on any structure assumed to be visible in the price path during this specific hour.

Standing backdrop: firm crude, 10Y near multi-year highs, payrolls Friday
No structural evidence assumed for this hour

Whether the Broadcom reaction has left European semiconductor names directional is the practical checkpoint for the following hours.

forecast.analysis: European cash open. The published score reflects the usual step-up in realised volatility at the open rather than an assumed direction. A gap that extends without a pullback through the first half hour would be the earliest evidence for a higher Tail path into the US session; an orderly open leaves the low band intact.

Bund and gilt yields leading Treasuries higher is the specific cross-asset alignment that would matter here, given how sensitive the index has been to the long end this week.

Crude is the standing swing factor: a fresh move through $92 WTI would raise Stress ahead of the US data block more than it would raise Tail.
